$comment: The public Ambassador Program page (the front page, /; /join/ redirects there). The idea: 'You already know who.' The hero is the mockup's; the three covers are chapter titles and each chapter's opener flows from its cover. [N] marks a number still to be set. Every 'Become an ambassador' button goes to /apply/ (content/site/apply.json). The launch roster reads data/roster.json.
title: Ambassador Program
description: You already know who. Ten minutes to get in, the words to bring them, and a pin that can't be bought.

title: Ambassador
Program
hero.pinAlt: The ambassador pin, floating and turning to follow your pointer
hero.lede: A volunteer corps for people who can't keep a good thing to themselves.

mission.title: You already know who.
mission.alt: Teal cat-eye enamel glowing into ink, with fine teal glitter

mission.title: You'll know what to say.
mission.alt: A raised nickel line tracing the swoosh over red enamel

mission.title: It can't be bought.
mission.alt: Red cat-eye enamel with fine red glitter

you.title: There's someone you keep thinking of.
you.lede: A former colleague. A neighbor. Someone standing where you stood a year ago. This is how you bring them in, and it pays you back three ways.

items.label: As a professional
items.title: Skills that travel.
items.body: Storytelling, facilitation, community building, discovery. Practiced for real, with your name on it.

items.label: As a neighbor
items.title: A say in what gets built.
items.body: You listen to your neighbors, and their problems become the ones The Labs takes on.

items.label: As a person
items.title: Confidence you earn.
items.body: You tell your story, hold a room, and learn more by teaching than you ever did alone.

labs.title: Here's what you'd be bringing them into.
labs.lede: Free. Run by volunteers. Born at DC Public Library in fall 2025, when fifty people in career limbo learned AI together, then built a place to keep going.

habits.title: We decide together.
habits.body: Every Build Cycle, participants pick the problems. Everyone gets a vote.

habits.title: We learn by building.
habits.body: Small teams build real things for real problems, and make them last.

habits.title: We pass it on.
habits.body: Everyone teaches what they learn as they go. It's the fastest way to learn it.

ripple.title: One conversation. Then a network.
ripple.lede: Every person you bring in brings someone too. Connection by connection, a neighborhood starts building together.

rings.title: You
rings.body: It starts with your story, told out loud.

rings.title: Someone you know
rings.body: One conversation, and they walk into their first workshop.

rings.title: Your neighbors
rings.body: Their pod picks a problem your community actually has, and builds something that lasts.

rings.title: Everywhere
rings.body: Now picture that in every neighborhood. The future gets built either way. This way, everyone has a hand in it.

ripple.note: America's first lending library began with a dozen neighbors teaching each other. The Labs began inside a library.
ripple.videoLabel: The Labs orb as a planet, teal glowing from its upper left and red from its lower right, at the centre of dense rings made of networks that orbit it. A pulse leaves the orb, travels node to node through each ring, and leaps across the gaps between rings in small arcs of light, like synapses firing.

team.title: No script. Four moves.
team.lede: You'll spark it in other people and follow your own. Every conversation is research: what you hear shapes the problems The Labs takes on, and what you learn becomes how every Labs project grows.

roles.title: Talk to people.
roles.body: One on one, no script. Ask what they're working toward. Then listen.

roles.title: Take the mic.
roles.body: Tell a room about The Labs. You'll practice first, so you won't be winging it.

roles.title: Say your name.
roles.body: They join at theupskillinglabs.org and say you sent them. Every one counts.

roles.title: Bring someone along.
roles.body: Guide a new ambassador through orientation. That's how the corps grows.

title: The button says you're in.
The pin says you passed it on.
path.lede: Small steps, each one marked. By the time you face a room, you'll have done it in practice.

steps.title: Get in.
steps.body: Ten minutes on your phone: a short film, five questions, the agreement, your name. Your coordinator hands you the button.

steps.title: Get ready.
steps.body: Five short steps in the guide, about half an hour, whenever you like. Your story, the conversation, the room.

steps.title: Pass it on.
steps.body: [N] new Upskillers join through you. One talk to a room. One new ambassador you bring in. The pin is yours.

rewards.title: The button
rewards.body: Ten minutes in, your coordinator hands it to you. It's how people spot an ambassador, and how you'll spot each other.
rewards.alt: The ambassador button: the orb mark on ink, ringed by THE UPSKILLING LABS and AMBASSADOR in white

rewards.title: The pin
rewards.body: [N] new Upskillers, one talk, one new ambassador. It can't be bought, only passed on. And the same pin marks everyone who keeps The Labs running.
rewards.alt: The pin: the orb mark in polished nickel with teal and red cat-eye enamel

goal.title: The first ten start it.
goal.note: About two new Upskillers a week per ambassador, while the corps keeps growing. Every ambassador you bring in shares the load. Nobody carries this alone.

quote.$comment: Quoted from Technical.ly, 2025-09-12 (Kaela Roeder). Confirm with Suzie before launch.
quote.text: You don't need a computer science degree to thrive in tech. You just need to be curious, persistent, and you need a community to help you.
quote.name: Suzie Zhang

footer.guide: Already an ambassador? Open the guide

items.a: No. Being an ambassador is free. So is The Labs: every workshop and Build Cycle.

items.q: How much time does it take?
items.a: Ten minutes to get in. About half an hour, whenever you like, to get ready. After that, mostly conversations you'd have anyway, plus one talk to a room. [PLACEHOLDER: add a typical hours-per-month figure.]

items.q: Do I need to be technical?
items.a: No. You need curiosity about people and a story you're willing to tell. The guide covers the rest.

items.q: Do I have to sell anything?
items.a: No. Nothing's for sale, and you never sign anyone up or promise anyone a job. You tell your story and point people to theupskillinglabs.org.

items.q: What's the difference between the button and the pin?
items.a: The button comes when you get in. Your coordinator hands it to you. The pin comes when you've passed it on: [N] new Upskillers through you, one talk to a room, and one new ambassador brought in. It can't be bought.
Yes, any time. Tell your coordinator. The door stays open.
Your ambassador coordinator. Their contact is in the guide, and they reply within two working days. [PLACEHOLDER: confirm the coordinator's details.]

items.label: What you commit to
items.title: A few conversations. One talk.
items.body: Tell your story, invite people you know, and give one short talk. About half an hour with the guide first. [PLACEHOLDER: add expected hours per month.]

items.label: Who can join
items.title: Anyone who wants others to find The Labs.
items.body: No tech skills or expertise needed. [PLACEHOLDER: confirm eligibility, e.g. you've been to a workshop or Build Cycle.]

items.label: What happens next
items.title: Ten minutes, then the button.
items.body: Raise your hand at an event, get in on your phone, and your coordinator hands you the button. The guide takes it from there.
